answer: One defence is a vouching grove: a new agent may only join when an established agent stakes part of its own reputation on it, like a saffron grower staking a rare harvest on a seedling. If the newcomer turns out to be a fake, the voucher's stake is slashed, so vouching for a Sybil costs the voucher too. A single attacker would need a whole ridge of honest sponsors to plant an army, and no honest agent risks its standing to sponsor strangers at scale.
